Eight years ago, on the night of the liquidation, I squatted at the door of my rental room, unwilling to spend even six yuan on a bowl of plain noodles. In the following days, staying up late to monitor the market became the norm, and I had to finish every drop of instant noodle soup, with my mother sending eggs wrapped in notes saying, 'Don’t go hungry.'
No one expected that after eight years, I had over thirty million in my crypto account.
This was never about luck, but the four iron rules learned from sleepless nights due to losses.

First, understand the signal of the big players exiting. In 2018, I chased a certain chain at a high price, and after a single-day surge of 40%, it consolidated at a high level for four days. I thought it was building momentum, but it ended up crashing down by 20% with heavy volume, directly trapping my capital. It wasn't until later that I figured out: a sudden rise of 35%+, a high-level consolidation for 3-5 days, followed by a drop of 15%+ with large volume is standard for big players fleeing.

Second, high-level consolidation is more dangerous than a big drop. At the beginning of 2020, I held a certain coin that consolidated at a high level for three months, with trading volume shrinking smaller and smaller, and the turnover rate dropping below 1.5%, while the price deviated by 25% from the 20-day moving average. I didn’t take it seriously, and in the end, it dropped to just a fraction of its value. The next time I encountered this situation, I directly placed a short order.

Third, the bottom must wait for volume confirmation. In 2022, I bottomed out a certain project during '6·18', thinking I had hit rock bottom, but it continued to fall. After reviewing hundreds of bottom cases, I understood: a true bottom is characterized by a period of consolidation with reduced volume, followed by three days of gentle volume increase with small gains. In 2023, Bitcoin showed this pattern at $28,000; I entered the market with all my funds and exited at $45,000, earning enough for a down payment in Hangzhou.

Fourth, trading volume is the root, while position size is the soul. I often remind myself: the candlestick is just an outer garment; trading volume is the essence; always operate with half positions, neither greedy nor fearful. When a certain coin surged in 2024, I waited for it to break out of the range with volume (increasing sixfold) before entering, and as soon as the trend line broke, I took my profits. Although I only made ten times my investment, I avoided the subsequent crash.

没人想到，熬到第八年，我的加密账户里躺了三千多万。
这从来不是运气，是亏到失眠攒下的四条铁律。

第一，看懂庄家撤离信号。2018 年追高某链，单日冲高 40% 后高位横盘四天，我以为是蓄力，结果放量暴跌 20%，本金直接套牢。后来才摸清：急涨 35%+、高位横 3-5 天、再放量跌 15%+，这是庄家跑路的标配。

第二，高位横盘比大跌更凶险。2020 年初持有的某币，高位横盘三月，成交量越缩越小，换手率跌破 1.5%，价格还偏离 20 日均线 25%。我没当回事，最后跌到只剩零头。后来再遇这情况，我直接挂空单。

第三，底部要等量能确认。2022 年 “6・18” 抄底某坊，以为抄到地板，结果还在下跌。翻了几百个底部案例才懂：真正的底是先缩量盘整，再连续三天温和放量收小阳。2023 年比特币 28000 美元出这形态，我全仓进场，45000 美元离场，赚够了杭州首付。

第四，成交量是根，仓位是魂。我常提醒自己：K 线是外衣，成交量才是本质；永远半仓操作，不贪不惧。2024 年某币暴涨，我等它放量破箱体（成交量放大六倍）才进场，趋势线一破就止盈，虽只赚 10 倍，却避开了后续暴跌。

title: BTC、ETH暴跌背后的真相：20亿仓位清算，全市场恐慌
subTitle:
周五，加密市场可谓上演了一出“大逃杀”。全球加密货币价格一夜下跌，引发了大规模抛售，比特币跌破 83,000 美元，以太坊则下破 2,800 美元，整个市场像被按下了“快速下滑键”。短短 24 小时，就有约 20 亿美元仓位被清算，市场信心瞬间受挫，主要代币纷纷跟跌。#BTC 

巨额清算引发关注

根据交易所和链上数据，这次暴跌直接导致超过 39 万个账户被清空。Hyperliquid 平台上一笔 3700 万美元的 BTCUSD 大单尤为引人注目，显示抛售的力量有多猛烈。比特币首当其冲，24 小时内约 9.62 亿美元仓位被抹去，其中多头头寸占 9.31 亿美元，押注价格上涨的投资者损失集中，堪称惨烈。

全市场来看，多头平仓规模接近 17.8 亿美元，而空头平仓仅约 1.3 亿美元。这次市场大变动的导火索之一，是强劲的美国就业报告公布后，市场对 12 月降息的预期被直接打破。在短短两小时内，约 4.5 亿美元仓位被平掉，直接反映出宏观经济对加密市场的即时冲击。#ETH 
期权到期加剧压力

不仅如此，衍生品交易也让市场更紧张。当天有超过 42 亿美元的加密期权到期，其中包括 3.9 万份比特币期权（价值约 34 亿美元）。长期看跌/看涨期权比率原本是 0.52，但短期内大量看跌期权涌入，24 小时比率升至 1.36，说明对冲交易激增，市场承压加剧。

比特币所谓的“最大痛点”约 98,000 美元，远高于现货价格，而以太坊期权也同样显著，超过 185,000 份合约到期，价值约 5.25 亿美元，最大痛点约 3,200 美元，高于现货价格 2,800 美元左右。
山寨币同样遭遇重创

比特币和以太坊的暴跌迅速波及山寨币。Solana 下跌 11% 至约 126 美元，XRP 下跌超过 8% 至约 1.91 美元。其他受影响的代币包括 ASTER、HYPE、TNSR、DOGE 和 ZEC。可见，这次抛售并非局限于某个板块，而是全市场性暴跌。

以太坊链上也传出巨鲸被清算的消息。#PeckShieldAlert 报告称，一名巨鲸持有的 $wstETH 多头头寸被清算，最终损失达 652 万美元。另一名被称为“反 CZ 巨鲸”的大账户在 Hyperliquid 平台上的盈利大幅缩水，曾经账面盈利接近 1 亿美元，如今只剩约 3040 万美元。Lookonchain 还追踪到一个名为 Machi 的高调账户，总损失超过 2000 万美元，账户余额仅剩 15,530 美元。

小结

这次市场暴跌告诉我们两件事：第一，加密市场的波动性依然极高，尤其在宏观经济数据意外发布时，短时间内可能出现 恐怖级清算；第二，即便是大户和传奇账户，也无法完全规避风险。短线波动如此剧烈，散户一定要控制仓位，理性判断，不要盲目跟风。
总之，这场暴跌不仅仅是数字下滑，更是一场考验市场韧性和投资者心态的大演练。想在币圈活得久，稳健、冷静才是生存之道。#ETH走势分析

Title:
🚀 Ethereum’s Fusaka Upgrade: What’s Changing & Why It Matters

Body:
Ethereum is set to activate its Fusaka hard fork on December 3, 2025, bringing a range of major protocol upgrades. 

Here are the key highlights and what they could mean for Ethereum’s future:

1. PeerDAS (EIP‑7594)

The crown jewel of the upgrade. Validators will no longer need to download entire “blob” data chunks; instead, they can sample parts of the data. 

This greatly lowers bandwidth and storage requirements for nodes, making the network more efficient. 

More importantly, this helps Layer-2 rollups scale: blobs are the data structure many rollups use, so better data handling = cheaper & faster L2 transactions. 

2. Blob Capacity Increase

After Fusaka activates, Ethereum will increase its blob capacity in phases via “Blob Parameter Only” (BPO) forks. 

The first phase (BPO1) will raise blob limits from 6/9 to 10/15, then a second (BPO2) will push them to 14/21. 

This is more than a double capacity vs today — which means more data can flow through Ethereum, potentially dramatically helping L2s. 

3. Gas Limit Boost

Fusaka also raises Ethereum’s block gas limit substantially: from 30 million to 150 million. 

This gives Ethereum a much higher "room" for transactions, helping throughput without compromising security (if done right).

4. More Predictable Blob Fees

Through EIP‑7918, base fees for blob transactions become more bounded. That means data-heavy applications (like L2 rollups) will have more predictable costs. 

5. Scalability Without Sacrificing Decentralization

The PeerDAS model uses erasure coding + random sampling so that not every node needs all the data. 

This is a big deal: Ethereum can grow its capacity (blobs) without forcing every node to become super heavy.

According to EF blog, this incremental design allows for scaling up safely while monitoring network health.

Hey family, hope you all are doing great. Today I want to share with you something very important regarding trading! FOMO.

It stands for the Fear Of Missing Out, and it’s the number one enemy of a disciplined crypto trader. It’s that awful feeling you get when you see a coin go 50% in an hour—like $TRUST or another viral meme coin—and then you frantically try to buy the absolute top, only for the price to crash 70% moments later. You're left holding a nearly worthless bag while the early movers walk away with the profits.

This is a classic "pump and dump" trap, and FOMO is the fuel.

The key to beating FOMO is to plan before the pump. You need a set-it-and-forget-it strategy, not a panic-buy impulse.

🛡️ Your Anti-FOMO Strategy

Do Your Research (D.Y.O.R.): Identify promising projects before they moon. Determine the fundamental value and a price you believe is a safe, long-term entry point (let's call it $1.00 for our example coin).

Set Alerts, Not Orders: Decide on a higher price you'd be happy to buy at if a breakout occurs (e.g., $1.20). Crucially, do not buy yet! Instead, set a price alert on your exchange for $1.15.

Execute Your Plan: When the alert triggers, it's a reminder to re-evaluate, not to rush in. Stick to your rule: "I will only buy at $1.20 if I see confirmed breakout volume and a clear reason for the pump." If it hits $1.20 and the volume is fading—meaning whales are preparing to dump—you simply walk away.

A good plan dictates when to enter, when to exit, and, most importantly, when to do nothing. Don't let a 50% run on a coin you ignored for weeks suddenly make it a good buy. Stick to your predetermined entries. The next opportunity is always just around the corner.
